newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares hit new record high.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares hit new record high.

text.p: The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at a new record on Monday, but traders noted a slight easing in the afternoon and said the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on May 20 could affect shares in the short term.
The RTS index rose to 366.22 on a total market turnover of $40.8 million. The previous record of 362.52 on a near-record market volume of $68.8 million was reached on May 16.
Dealers said New York investors were more inclined to sell on Monday but that neither selling nor buying volumes were significant.

"We're waiting for news first of all from the U.S. If there is no rise in interest rates then it's possible the market will continue to grow, perhaps even faster than before," said one trader who asked not to be named.
"But if they raise rates then we would have to start talking about a new investor strategy -- the playing field would be different."
But the trader said the Russian market's consolidation in the last few hours of trading was more of a correction than a result of rate hike fears.
The Fed will meet on Tuesday and some investors fear it could raise interest rates, although recent economic indicators have given a mixed picture of the state of the U.S. economy.

National electricity utility UES EESR.RTS eased to $0.3172 from $0.3200 previously, while regional power company Mosenergo MSNG.RTS slid to $1.329 from $1.364. Oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS slipped to $14.82 from $15.04.
But Regent European Securities vice-president Dmitry Starenko said there would be only a limited Russian market reaction to any interest rate decision.

"The closer we get to the interest rate announcement, the more people are placing their bets. If rates aren't raised in the States, people will hurry to buy, if they raise them there could be either a little stagnation or a slight fall," he said.
"In either case, I don't expect significant fluctutions."
